papers.title: Graph Attention Networks
papers.abstract: Graph Attention Networks use masked self-attentional layers to assign different weights to neighboring nodes. The model combines local graph neighborhoods with attention-based message passing and was evaluated on graph benchmarks.

papers.title: Graph Transformers: A Generalization of Transformers to Graphs
papers.abstract: Graph Transformers extend attention beyond local neighborhoods using structural encodings and global interactions between nodes. The paper discusses computational cost and graph structure bias.

papers.title: Graph Attention Networks
papers.abstract: Graph attention assigns learned importance to adjacent nodes. Neighborhood attention supports inductive node representation learning and avoids requiring the full graph during inference.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
papers.abstract: Graph convolutional networks learn node representations by aggregating information from local neighborhoods. The method provides a scalable baseline for semi-supervised graph learning.

papers.title: Graph Transformers: A Generalization of Transformers to Graphs
papers.abstract: This work studies graph transformers that model global attention alongside structural graph information. It highlights trade-offs between expressivity, structural bias, and computational complexity.

papers.title: Efficient Graph Attention with Sparse Neighborhoods
papers.abstract: Sparse neighborhood attention reduces the cost of graph attention on large graphs. Experiments show that locality and sampling choices affect accuracy and runtime.
